fact: Challenge.ma reports that no approval for Starlink has been announced by the ANRT in Morocco; only a legal entity has been created and administrative preparations begun since 2024, so Starlink is not yet licensed.

Maroc Hebdo reports Starlink Internet Services Morocco was created in Casablanca, but final approvals from the ANRT and the DGSSI are still to be obtained before commercial launch, so no licence is held.

Medias24 reports Starlink is not officially authorised by the ANRT, negotiations continue, and per an expert Moroccans may not subscribe to Starlink in Morocco; existing users hold European subscriptions, and use is outside the licensing regime. ANRT did not respond.
Morocco is listed among about 34 countries where Starlink sits in regulatory limbo, neither approved nor explicitly banned, as of June 2026 per CIO Africa; no licence is stated.

The minister said any customer in areas without terrestrial broadband can get financial support of up to 2,500 dirhams per subscription to satellite internet from an approved provider under the VSAT initiative.

The ministry states that under the VSAT initiative citizens and firms in areas without terrestrial coverage can take a satellite internet subscription subsidised 50 per cent by the universal service fund up to 2,500 DH, with over 2,500 access points subsidised by end 2022.

Minister Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni said on 20 April 2026 that VSAT satellite technology is used in zones hard to serve by terrestrial networks, with each customer eligible for MAD 2,500 support per subscription, up to 4,000 beneficiaries a year.
